title: Votes on matters that name an interest the member had declared
question: Where roll calls exist, did a member of the Planning Commission, Historic Preservation Commission or Board of Appeals vote on a matter that names a business, investment or income source on the member's own Form 700?
finding: 2,336 recorded votes were tested against the declarations of 60 members. 3 votes named a declared interest, none of them a business the member owns or is paid by: all 3 concern shares in a large public company whose branch or shop was the subject of the application. In 1 matter naming a declared interest the member is recorded as recused. On this test the record shows nothing unusual.
how: Every action with a printed roll call in the Planning Commission and Historic Preservation Commission minutes (April 2018 to August 2022) and the Board of Appeals minutes (September 2022 to November 2026). The item's printed description, and for appeals the permit holder and permit description, are searched for the whole name of each entity the voting or recused member declared on Schedule A-1, A-2 or C for the year of the vote or the year either side. The City and other public bodies as income sources are left out, as are one-word names.
limits: The minutes describe a project by address and use; they rarely name the owner, developer, architect or lender, so a member's interest in a party that the minutes do not name cannot be found this way. The one settled case of this kind on the Ethics Commission's list, a Planning Commissioner who voted on projects designed by the firm paying her retirement income, does not appear here although she declared the firm as an income source every year: the minutes on file never name that firm, so the test could not see it. Real property near a project (Schedule B) is not tested. Whether a shareholding in a large public company bars a member from a routine permit for one of its branches depends on thresholds in State rules that are not in these files, and the declared range of the holding is shown. Private applicants and appellants are not searched or named.
